data.body:
A TOML descriptor loaded into the RecordKind registry (P-record-contract, P-extension-seams.registry); Python only for kinds with behaviour; about 15 new kinds (requirement, stakeholder, vendor, contract, risk, comm log, assumption, fitness function, proposal types, attestation, attention item) become rows; user-defined kinds follow; conformance test (B-rc-conformance) runs over data kinds too.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds (kind, template, gate, lens, role, lint set, importer, pack, job) is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

Split into: SE-kind-data.1, SE-kind-data.2, SE-kind-data.3.

chunk_findings.detail: `records.py` executes `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` (and immediately calls `load_packaged("rule")`) while `record_kind_data` is still mid-import, so the two modules can only be imported in the order "records first". Given the reverse order, the chain is: `import ddflow.api.record_kind_data` → its top-level `from . import records as R` starts executing `records.py` → `records.py` reaches `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` → `record_kind_data` is in `sys.modules` but partially initialized (`load_packaged` is defined *after* the `from . import records` line, so it has not been bound yet) → CPython raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'load_packaged' from partially initialized module 'ddflow.api.record_kind_data' (most likely due to a circular import)`. Concretely, `python -c "import ddflow.api.record_kind_data"` — or any test/loader module whose first ddflow import is `from ddflow.api.record_kind_data import parse_kind, packaged`, which is the natural way to exercise this new file — fails at import time as long as `ddflow/api/__init__.py` does not itself import `records` first. Placing the import mid-file with `# noqa: E402` only satisfies the linter; it does not break the cycle. Moving the `records` import inside the three functions (or having `records` import `load_packaged` lazily inside a function rather than at module scope) would remove the order dependency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py:26 (`from . import records as R`)

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring states the loader's central safety invariant: "Python is for kinds with behaviour (`ops`, `weakening`); a descriptor naming either is refused." Nothing in the diff enforces this. `kind_from_data` copies the parsed descriptor verbatim (`args = dict(desc)`), rewrites only `fields`, `declined`, `export` and `feed`, and then calls `R.RecordKind(**args)`. Since `RecordKind` is the same class that behaviour kinds use to carry `ops`/`weakening` (the docstring itself implies these keys are nameable on this structure), a descriptor such as `ops = ["ddflow.something"]` or `weakening = true` is not refused — it is accepted and passed straight into the kind, i.e. a data-only TOML descriptor can smuggle in the behaviour the loader is documented to keep in Python. The stated refusal is a check that was never written, so the guarantee callers will rely on ("a kind with no behaviour needs no Python") does not hold for these two keys.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py (`kind_from_data`, module docstring)

chunk_findings.detail: `D.register_kind(args["def_kind"], args["summary"])` is invoked *before* `R.RecordKind(**args)`, and `register_kind` mutates the global `defs.DEF_KINDS` via `setdefault`. Any descriptor that gets past the field/verb/export rewriting but then fails construction (e.g. an unexpected key such as `bogus = "x"`, or a missing required `name`, making `RecordKind(**args)` raise `TypeError`) has already permanently added its `def_kind` to `DEF_KINDS`. Concrete input: `parse_kind('name="?" ...')` on a descriptor whose only problem is an extra key leaves `defs.DEF_KINDS["<new def_kind>"]` present even though no kind was ever declared and the caller saw an exception; a subsequent parse of a corrected descriptor, or any later code that trusts `DEF_KINDS`, now sees a definition kind that was never successfully created. Moving the registration after successful construction (or rolling it back on failure) would remove the failed-parse leak.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py:54 (`kind_from_data` -> `D.register_kind`)

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier report stands: `record_kind_data.py` does `from . import records as R` at module scope, and `records.py` executes `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` at module scope and immediately calls it. Whichever module is imported first forces the other to be executed while the first is still partially initialized. Concretely, `python -c "import ddflow.api.record_kind_data"` starts executing `record_kind_data.py`, reaches line 26, runs `records.py`, which reaches `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` against the partially-initialized module — resolving only if `load_packaged` happens to be bound above line 26; otherwise this raises ImportError, so the two modules are only importable in the order "records first". The triage for this item is still `untriaged` and the portion of the diff shown here (the new `ddflow/templates/kinds/rule.toml` descriptor) contains no change to either module, so nothing in this part of the change answers the finding.

chunk_findings.detail: The two file-discovery helpers in this new module disagree about what a descriptor's "name" is, so composing them the obvious way fails at runtime. `packaged()` yields `entry.name`, i.e. the file name including the extension (`"<name>.toml"`, per its own docstring "`(file name, text)` of every packaged descriptor"), whereas `load_packaged(name)` builds its path as `KINDS_DIR / f"{name}.toml"`, i.e. it expects the bare kind name. Given the packaged descriptors on disk, a caller that enumerates `for fname, text in packaged(): load_packaged(fname)` (the natural way to load everything the module advertises) reads `ddflow/templates/kinds/<name>.toml.toml` and raises `FileNotFoundError`, and there is nothing in either signature or docstring that tells the caller to strip the suffix. Either `packaged()` should yield `entry.stem`, or `load_packaged` should accept a name that may already carry `.toml`.
